cover.title: Recoil Report, Justin Delaney / Louisville Brands
cover.subtitle: Reverse Listening + Deep Recall on the first Justin call. Genuine product resonance, a real receipt co-built live, a warm park behind a heads-down focus gate, and a same-day champion text that widened the prize past Louisville.
cover.meta: ARCS RECOIL · Jul 31, 2026 · ~50 min intro call · Justin Delaney (Louisville Brands CEO) · Jeben Berg (champion) · no PrepSession captured

loadBearingQuote.text: One of the reasons I didn't want to be on video is because I was going to work on [the Japan JV] while I listened to you, because I usually do two things at once. And thanks for this moment of focus. It's been nice.
loadBearingQuote.attribution: Justin Delaney, unprompted, near the close · Jul 31, 2026

callWalk.label: 0–10 min · Rapport
callWalk.title: Connecticut, Brooklyn, the golden temple, and a graffiti cautionary tale
callWalk.body: Long, easy rapport: shared New York / Connecticut geography, the Brooklyn-exports-itself thesis, and a deep Japanophile thread (Zach's honeymoon at the golden temple, Justin's whiskey and JV history in Japan). Justin is outside with his daughters running a lemonade-and-Pumps content stunt out front. He agrees to move to a screen and, notably, to go on camera: 'I usually don't do video, but you can have it.' First tell that this call is already off his default rails.

callWalk.label: 10–15 min · The frame
callWalk.title: Jeben hands off the thesis and widens the aperture past Louisville
callWalk.body: Jeben frames ARCS as 'a very impactful tool for decision making inside of an organization' and immediately broadens it: 'there could be something with Louisville Brands, but it doesn't have to be.' He points at his own network and an academic lead-gen funnel (he teaches business-school organizational design). The champion is carrying the thread, but he is deliberately de-risking the specific Louisville ask into a general 'meet Zach, see what he's up to.'

callWalk.label: 15–28 min · The walkthrough
callWalk.title: Decision receipts, the board of agents, kintsugi, dual bar-raiser
callWalk.body: Zach walks louisville.arcs.care live: the receipt as a circuit-breaker (assumptions, risks, exit rule, signed and revisited), the board of divergent agent perspectives, the kintsugi 'case against,' and the stoic-vs-cynic dual bar-raiser. Justin tracks it closely and starts co-designing out loud: 'you could adjust these in priority... more weight on the elder.' He is not being sold to; he is already modeling the mechanic.

callWalk.label: 28–34 min · The admission
callWalk.title: The vulnerability job-to-be-done, in Justin's own words
callWalk.body: Justin names the emotional need ARCS serves: 'as a leader, that's the issue, you have your own biases, and then you have all these other people you discount completely to zero... this gives you a way to do that in a candid way that doesn't feel as vulnerable as going around asking everyone for advice, it sometimes ends up making you look weak.' He reveals a heavy DIY stack (OpenClaw, Hermes, mythos, Manus, and 'CIC' data lakes) and admits 'I kind of do this already.'

callWalk.label: 34–42 min · The live receipt
callWalk.title: Justin co-builds a real vendor tripwire with his own numbers
callWalk.body: The product lands hardest here. Justin volunteers a live decision: a national sales team at $12K/mo he wants adding ~$150K revenue/month, and he articulates the tripwire himself, 'by October, if not generating incrementality of $120K/month, we put in end-of-year notice; over $150 we RFP; over $200 we let it roll, maybe a bonus.' Then he sharpens it past binary: drop the retainer to $5K, raise commission, target the two regions they actually win. This is the walked pitch path working exactly as designed.

callWalk.label: 42–50 min · Japan + the tell
callWalk.title: The camera confession, and the real constraint surfaces
callWalk.body: Talk turns to the Japan JV (contract distillery, True Essence, a partner named Cogent). Justin then delivers the load-bearing line: he did not want video because he'd planned to work on the JV while half-listening, 'I usually do two things at once,' and thanks Zach for 'this moment of focus.' In the same breath he states the constraint: 'everything we're doing, the one thing we have going on, is working so well that we're just like, let's just focus on this. Once we level off and start adding headcount we'll probably look at some of these other things.'

callWalk.label: Close
callWalk.title: Warm, genuine, and parked, no date, no artifact requested
callWalk.body: Jeben re-frames the purpose explicitly: 'I wanted this to be an introductory call so you got a sense of what Zach's up to... I want you to synthesize and process it.' Justin is effusive ('really cool, awesome, I think it's awesome') and open to collaborating 'professionally or in an academic context or through the network of networks,' then exits to another meeting. Read forward, the call built toward a paid session; read backward, it landed on 'intro call, synthesize it, we're heads-down.' No next date, no artifact requested.

signalThreads.label: Post-call, in writing
signalThreads.title: Jeben confirmed it within the hour, and widened the prize
signalThreads.body: Minutes after the call Jeben texted: 'That was a great call, you were really on point and he and I will discuss. The real goal of this is maybe something with Louisville Brands but also I want to see about getting you placed inside of some other businesses that are much larger with infinite funding.' Then: 'He has deeper access than I do.' The champion is not just warm, he is actively brokering, he and Justin will discuss, and he is repositioning Zach past Louisville toward larger, better-funded orgs, with Justin himself named as the deeper-access connector.
signalThreads.note: This reframes the target: Louisville is one door; the bigger prize is placement into Justin's and Jeben's larger network. Keep Louisville concrete (the October receipt) while letting Jeben run the bigger-org play.

signalThreads.label: Product resonance
signalThreads.title: He didn't just get it, he built one live with real numbers
signalThreads.body: Justin co-created a vendor tripwire receipt on the call using his own figures ($12K/mo sales team, +$150K target, an October renewal gate) and then improved the mechanic himself (graduated retainer/commission by region, not a binary fire/keep). Repeated unprompted praise: 'this is really cool,' 'I love this,' 'it's awesome.'
signalThreads.note: This is the strongest possible product signal: the buyer operated the product on his own live decision. It also means he understands it well enough to under-value it (see build-vs-buy).

signalThreads.label: The real job-to-be-done
signalThreads.title: Objectivity without looking weak
signalThreads.body: Two of his own lines carry the positioning: 'it'd be nice to know what the objectivity is based on the decision we made and the expectations at the beginning, as opposed to the emotion, which is how so often things are governed,' and the board 'gives you a way to [get outside input] in a candid way that doesn't feel as vulnerable... going around asking everyone for advice sometimes ends up making you look weak.'
signalThreads.note: Lead future contact with the emotional job (candid outside read, no loss of face), not the feature list. That is the wedge he named.

signalThreads.label: The focus moment
signalThreads.title: The camera did the thing the product promises
signalThreads.body: Justin's default is documented, by his own admission: multitask, decide fast on instinct, two things at once. Going on camera pulled him into a single-threaded hour and he noticed and thanked Zach for it. This is a live proof of the ARCS thesis (structure beats distracted instinct) and a direct confirmation of the pain Jeben described in discovery.
signalThreads.note: Also a caution: the slow lane is not his default. Adoption depends on him choosing focus again without a camera forcing it.

signalThreads.label: Timing gate
signalThreads.title: Heads-down on Japan, 'let's just focus on this'
signalThreads.body: The single biggest constraint, stated plainly: the current bet (the Japan JV / core business) is working so well they are deliberately not adding new things until they level off and add headcount. This is not a no. It is a real 'not now' with a named condition.
signalThreads.note: The next step must ride an existing must-decide moment (the October sales-team renewal he already scoped), not ask him to add ARCS as a new initiative.

signalThreads.label: Champion posture
signalThreads.title: Jeben carries it, but widened it past Louisville
signalThreads.body: Jeben opened and closed by broadening ARCS beyond Louisville Brands into his network and an academic funnel, and framed the call as introductory. That protects the relationship and opens more doors, but it also removes a single owner and a specific Louisville next step.
signalThreads.note: Confirmed by his same-day text (see 'Post-call, in writing'): keep Jeben fed with the network / larger-org angle he is actively working, and drive the concrete Louisville step directly with Justin.

signalThreads.label: Resonance channel
signalThreads.title: The sake wedge: seimaibuai, no false binaries, and a signal too good to export
signalThreads.body: Justin is a serious connoisseur: whiskey barrels, sake, Ichiro's malts, and a Japan contract-distillery JV filled the back half of the call. That is the OM carrier, and three sake truths each carry the ARCS thesis in his native register. One, seimaibuai: daiginjo is rice milled to a quarter of itself, everything non-essential polished away until only the pure core signal remains, which is exactly what a decision receipt does to a decision. Two, the hot-versus-cold false dichotomy: some sake is only itself served cold, and forcing the binary ruins it, the same trap Justin named himself when he pushed his vendor call past fire-or-keep into a graduated, region-by-region read. Three, the finest sake never leaves Japan because it would not be appreciated abroad, his own frustration on the call: the 100 percent signal survives only where there is a palate to receive it, which is precisely the loss ARCS's scored, revisitable record is built to prevent.
signalThreads.note: This is the one register that lands by constructive interference, not pitch. Carry the next touch on it: seimaibuai for judgment, no false binaries, and a signal too good to lose in translation, harmonized with the omakase canon.

best.title: Justin runs the sales-team receipt he already half-built, before the October gate
best.body: Zach sends back the exact vendor tripwire Justin co-created (the $12K/mo team, the $120K/$150K/$200K bands, the October renewal), rendered as a receipt he can seal in one click. Because it maps to a real decision already on his calendar, he takes the 60–90 minute live session on that single call.
best.note: Already partly in motion: Jeben texted 'he and I will discuss' within the hour. Signal to watch: a proposed time, or Jeben routing Zach into one of the 'larger, infinite-funding' orgs he named.

base.title: It parks as 'synthesize and process,' kept alive by one dated hook
base.body: Justin stays heads-down on Japan, but Jeben actively carries the thread, he said he and Justin will discuss and wants Zach placed in larger orgs. It advances on Jeben's brokering plus one low-friction dated artifact tied to Justin's October renewal, rather than an open 'let's collaborate.'
base.note: The failure mode inside base case is a vague follow-up ('great to meet, let's find ways to work together') that gives him nothing to act on.

worst.title: It diffuses into network/academic vibes with no owner and no date
worst.body: The thread dissolves into 'other businesses,' academic funnels, and Japan-whiskey camaraderie; Justin's own AI stack absorbs the felt need; the specific Louisville next step never gets a date. The thread goes quiet.
worst.note: Downside is fully capped: no spend, relationship intact, Jeben still a champion, and Justin left with a genuinely good impression. The only unforced error is over-pursuing against his stated 'let's just focus on this.'

riskFlags.label: Timing / focus gate
riskFlags.body: 'Everything is working, let's just focus on this... once we level off and add headcount.' The biggest gate. Any next step that reads as a new initiative dies here; only riding his existing October decision survives it.

riskFlags.label: Build-vs-buy
riskFlags.body: Justin is a sophisticated AI power user who already DIYs multi-perspective critique (persona coaches on his book) and runs a CIC/mythos data stack. He said 'I kind of do this already.' Risk: he under-values the receipt discipline (the scoring, the compounding record, the pre-committed exit) or assumes his stack replicates it. Differentiate on the disciplined, scored, revisited record, not on 'AI gives you perspectives.'

riskFlags.label: No committed next step
riskFlags.body: The call ended warm but with no scheduled session, no artifact requested, and no date, 'synthesize and process it.' Enthusiasm without a commitment. Requires Zach to manufacture the next step, once, with a specific dated hook.

riskFlags.label: Attention default is distracted
riskFlags.body: By his own admission Justin normally does two things at once and decides fast on instinct. The camera created a rare focused hour. Product adoption asks him to choose that slow lane deliberately; design the first session so the focus is structurally enforced (a live, timeboxed, single-decision working session), the way the camera enforced it here.

riskFlags.label: Champion diffusion
riskFlags.body: Jeben broadened the ask into his network and academia and called it an intro. Good for surface area, but it softens the Louisville-specific next step. Manage as two tracks: Justin's own October receipt (concrete), and Jeben's network/academic angle (long-tail).

protocol.label: Step 1
protocol.title: Send back the receipt he already built, anchored to October
protocol.body: One artifact: the sales-team vendor tripwire Justin co-created live, rendered as a sealed-ready receipt with his own bands ($120K notice / $150K RFP / $200K roll) and the October renewal date. Frame: 'here's the one you started, want to run it live before the October call?' Ride his real decision, do not ask him to adopt a new thing.

protocol.label: Step 2
protocol.title: Lead with the job he named, carried on the sake metaphor
protocol.body: In the note, use his own language, objectivity vs emotion and a candid outside read without looking weak, and carry it on the resonance channel he opened: a receipt polishes a decision the way daiginjo polishes rice to its 25th level, milling away everything that is not the essence until only the 100% signal remains. It speaks his connoisseur register and lands by constructive interference with the omakase canon, not by another feature list. Keep it to a few lines; he is a fast reader who is heads-down.

protocol.label: Step 3
protocol.title: Honor the focus gate, one hook, then let it breathe
protocol.body: He said 'let's just focus on this.' Send the single dated hook, then stop pursuing. Rising effort against his stated heads-down is the alarm (the active-listening rule). If the sales-team session lands, it lands on his timeline; if not, the relationship and the impression are intact.

protocol.label: Step 4
protocol.title: Feed the champion the angle he volunteered
protocol.body: Give Jeben the compact, forwardable version aimed at his network and the academic lead-gen funnel he raised, so the thread stays alive beyond Louisville while Justin is heads-down. Keep the two tracks separate so neither dilutes the other.

protocol.label: Step 5
protocol.title: Score this call as its own receipt
protocol.body: There was no PrepSession, so no ex-ante baseline was captured. File this recoil as the scoring artifact: the pre-call read (intro, Jeben-brokered, low expectation) vs. what actually happened (deep product resonance, a live co-built receipt, a warm park behind a focus gate). Capture a real ex-ante receipt before the next Justin touch so the next recoil scores against a written expectation, not just revealed signal.

kinematics.caption: Resonance gradient across the call, the memory bookmarks: where the signal peaked (kairos) and where he parked. Read it like an Observatory replay, the two peaks are where to re-enter the conversation, the park is the gate to respect.
